### The baselines' reference configurations with unit-direction wings {#sec-oq-reference-selection}

```{python}
#| label: para-oq-reference-selection
#| output: asis
SEL = json.load(open(RES / "char" / "ref80_select_2026-10-03.json"))["datasets"]
def sel(arch, cand, ds):
    return SEL[ds][arch]["candidates"][cand]["pressure_l2"]
GT_REF, GT_BIG = "gt_h256", "gt_h1024_c100k"        # width 256 at 200,000 cells (the reference); width 1,024 at 100,000 cells
T_REF, T_CAR = "t_h512_l16_c100k", "t_h1024_c100k"  # width 512, 16 layers (the reference); width 1,024; both at 100,000 cells
assert SEL["drivaer_surface"]["GeoTransolver"]["winner"] == GT_BIG and SEL["hilift_210"]["GeoTransolver"]["winner"] == GT_REF
assert SEL["drivaer_surface"]["Transolver"]["winner"] == T_CAR and SEL["hilift_210"]["Transolver"]["winner"] == T_REF
print("**The open question is whether GeoTransolver and Transolver keep their reference configurations when the selection's wings give "
      "them the unit direction.** The selection scored every candidate on the DrivAerML Surface task and on HiLiftAeroML at 510 training "
      "cases (@sec-selection), and on the wings the baselines read the freestream in inch/s, which costs them on this rung (@tbl-hilift-unit-drive). Under the 80 GiB budget, "
      f"GeoTransolver at width 1,024 trained on 100,000 cells has a surface pressure error of {sel('GeoTransolver', GT_BIG, 'drivaer_surface'):.4f} "
      f"on the DrivAerML Surface task against {sel('GeoTransolver', GT_REF, 'drivaer_surface'):.4f} for the reference width 256, and "
      f"{sel('GeoTransolver', GT_BIG, 'hilift_210'):.3f} against {sel('GeoTransolver', GT_REF, 'hilift_210'):.3f} on the wings, which cost it "
      "the joint score. Transolver's reference, width 512 with 16 layers, also owes its place to the wings: width 1,024 wins on the cars, "
      f"{sel('Transolver', T_CAR, 'drivaer_surface'):.4f} against {sel('Transolver', T_REF, 'drivaer_surface'):.4f} and at lower memory, both trained "
      "at 100,000 cells and scored at 200,000 as every candidate of the selection (@sec-selection), and trails on the wings, "
      f"{sel('Transolver', T_CAR, 'hilift_210'):.4f} against {sel('Transolver', T_REF, 'hilift_210'):.4f} (@tbl-selection). If the wing "
      "ranking is an artifact of the raw vector, the baselines' reference configurations, and every standing scored with them, may change. "
      "What would settle it: the GeoTransolver and Transolver candidates of @tbl-selection retrained on the 510 wing cases reading the unit "
      "direction, two seeds each, and the registered rule applied again. Cost: not priced, because the wing rung is not in the cost record. "
      "Data: results/char/ref80_select_2026-10-03.json.")
```

```{python}
      "(@sec-capacity). The reference configurations sit above the floor those ladders reach (@sec-shared-floor), and the fitted law, "
      "evaluated at the reference ISLA's parameters and 435 cars, predicts a lower error than the reference measures (@fig-iso-compute). "
      "Both gaps could be the instrument or the configuration. What would settle it: on the DrivAerML Surface task, the five case rungs "
      f"at three sizes around the reference configuration, two seeds each ({fmt_h(q5_ladder)} GPU-hours, each run's epoch proportional "
      f"to its cases and every size priced at the reference's {ref_lane:.0f} GPU-hours a run, a lower bound for the larger sizes), and a "
      f"cell ladder of 100,000, 200,000 and 400,000 cells at 435 cars ({fmt_h(q5_cells)} GPU-hours, priced in proportion to cells); "
```

### The Tensile2d deficit {#sec-oq-tensile2d}

```{python}
#| label: para-oq-tensile2d
#| output: asis
t = ST["tensile2d"]
WD = {"stress_l2": "stress", "displacement_l2": "displacement", "q_l2": "plastic strain"}
worst_r = min(((ST[k].ratio(b, f), k, f, b) for k in FIN for f in ST[k].ds.headline for b in S.BASELINES if ST[k].compared(b, f)))
by_fields = {}
for b in S.BASELINES:
    fs = " and ".join(WD[f] for f in t.ds.headline if t.verdict(b, f) == "trails")
    if fs:
        by_fields.setdefault(fs, []).append(b)
trails = [f"{' and '.join(bs)} on {fs}" for fs, bs in by_fields.items()]
print(f"**The open question is what causes ISLA's deficit on PLAID Tensile2d.** ISLA trails {' and '.join(trails)} (@sec-tensile2d): "
      f"GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA reads {r('tensile2d', 'GeoTransolver', 'stress_l2'):.2f} on stress and "
      f"{r('tensile2d', 'GeoTransolver', 'displacement_l2'):.2f} on displacement, Transolver ÷ ISLA {r('tensile2d', 'Transolver', 'stress_l2'):.2f} "
      f"and {r('tensile2d', 'Transolver', 'displacement_l2'):.2f}, on a metric dominated by specimens that never yield, with ISLA's "
      f"{SEEDW[t.n_seeds('ISLA')]} seeds far apart. The smallest ratio of the {n_all} comparisons is {worst_r[0]:.2f}, {worst_r[3]} on "
      f"{WD.get(worst_r[2], worst_r[2])}; {NOTE[0].lower() + NOTE[1:] if NOTE else ''} Its interior geometry is exact here and its pose contract holds (@sec-limits-ties), and an "
      "ablation of ISLA against itself finds no accuracy cost in any of the changes from an earlier form of its code, with its "
      "prediction-point embedding the better design on this dataset (@tbl-tensile2d-attrib). Two candidate causes remain. One is the "
      "aggregation: GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation) isolates whether the quadrature weighting costs accuracy "
      "on a mesh whose boundary segments are nearly equal. The other is positional resolution: one specimen family barely moves the "
      "slice anchors between cases, so a point's position is known only as finely as the partition (@sec-vs-novel-anchors). What would "
      f"settle it: the ablation at two seeds on the reference protocol, and ISLA's error per node set beside the baselines'. Cost: "
      f"{fmt_h(q6)} GPU-hours.")
```

## Datasets beyond external aerodynamics {#sec-limits-datasets}

```{python}
#| label: para-limits-datasets
#| output: asis
SOL = [k for k in ("tensile2d", "lug", "deepjeb") if k in ST]
def sline(k):
    s = ST[k]
    cav = " (Transolver reads no boundary-condition labels there)" if k == "lug" else ""
    flight = " (in flight, @sec-ledger)" if s.in_flight else ""
    return f"{s.ds.name}{flight}: " + ", ".join(f"{field_name(s, f)} ISLA {s.verdict('GeoTransolver', f)} GeoTransolver and {s.verdict('Transolver', f)} Transolver"
                                        for f in s.ds.headline) + cav
print("**Three structural-mechanics problems carry standings beside the aerodynamic ones, and they read in both directions.** "
      + "; ".join(sline(k) for k in SOL) + " (@sec-tensile2d, @sec-lug, @sec-deepjeb). These sets were chosen for varying boundary "
      "conditions and loads, not only varying geometry, so that the global-scalar, global-vector and boundary-input channels are "
      "exercised. Whether the interface carries to further steady boundary-driven PDEs, heat conduction or electrostatics for example, "
      "is unmeasured. AeroZoo, the diversity benchmark within aerodynamics, holds its standing in @sec-interior-aerozoo; its open "
      "questions are @sec-oq-dtt, @sec-oq-aerozoo and @sec-oq-outlet.")
```

## Engineering directions {#sec-future}

```{python}
#| label: make-tbl-future
#| output: asis
step = lambda k, a: S.cost(k, a)["step_seconds"]
small = {k: [step(k, "ISLA") / step(k, b) for b in S.BASELINES] for k in ("tensile2d", "lug")}
lo, hi = min(min(v) for v in small.values()), max(max(v) for v in small.values())
print("**Four directions are engineering rather than research: each has a measured starting point and a stated remainder.**")
print()
print("| direction | what is in place | what remains |\n|---|---|---|")
print("| Problems outside external aerodynamics | the interface accepts zero or more global vector inputs, zero or more global scalar "
      "inputs and per-cell boundary data of declared tensor rank (@sec-isla-inputs); the contract tests cover zero and two global "
      "directions | a production dataset outside external aerodynamics with a baseline trained on it under the fair-comparison protocol "
      "(@sec-limits-datasets) |")
print("| Cost on small meshes | from 100,000 tokens up a training step's memory is linear in tokens for every reference configuration and "
      "its time on the surface task (@sec-cost-sweep) | on the small finite-element meshes of Tensile2d and the lug ISLA's median "
      f"training step is {lo:.1f} to {hi:.1f} times the baselines' (@tbl-ref-cost); a profile of those training runs would locate the gap |")
print("| Inference on a small budget | the stratified sampler removes most of the quadrature variance at 10,000 cells "
      "(@sec-deficit-anatomy, @sec-using-sampler) | a default that picks the sampler from the requested count |")
print("| Query-count consistency of the interacting form | the prediction points' routing mass is a learned fraction of the boundary "
      "measure, independent of their count (@sec-isla-contracts) | a prediction at a point independent of the request at the "
      "interacting form's accuracy, or the read-only form as the default (@sec-oq-dtt) |")
print()
print(": The engineering directions: what is in place for each and what remains. How to read this: each row is a direction with a "
      "measured starting point, not a research question; the open questions with a measurement that would settle them are "
      "@tbl-open-questions. Data: results/char/cost_090.json. {#tbl-future}")
```

## What would change the recommendation {#sec-review-roads}

```{python}
#| label: para-review-roads
#| output: asis
print("**ISLA is the choice where the deployment mesh or sampling law may differ from the training one, where geometries arrive in "
      "arbitrary poses, and where a surrogate must be a function of the physics rather than of the dataset's frame; on in-distribution "
      f"accuracy at matched memory it leads in {len(TAL['leads'])}{LUGC}, is level in {len(TAL['is level with'])} and trails in "
      f"{len(TAL['trails'])} of the {n_all} comparisons of the final standings (@sec-standing).** " + NOTE + " The recommendation rests on the contracts, "
      "not on an accuracy lead. They hold on every standing up to three measured limits: the closest-feature ties of the lug's mesh, "
      "a candidate cause of its posed growth whose link is not isolated (@sec-limits-ties), the interacting form's dependence on the request (@sec-limits-query-independence), and the precision of the "
      "wall the interior model is given (@sec-limits-boundary-law, @sec-oq-precision). GeoTransolver and Transolver are released, in "
      "use and not modified; measure weighting and origin-free positions reach users through ISLA (@sec-principled-ledger). Three "
      "outcomes would change the recommendation.")
print()
print("- **The interior model changes form** unless interacting ISLA is clearly the more accurate on AeroZoo's held-out splits "
      "(@sec-oq-dtt): the recommendation is then a read-only model whose prediction at a point depends on that point and the "
      "boundary alone.")
print("- **ISLA gains a generalization claim on velocity** if its held-out penalty on AeroZoo velocity stays below a converged "
      "GeoTransolver's; on pressure no claim is possible while both baselines sit at the zero predictor (@sec-limits-transfer, "
      "@sec-aerozoo-baselines).")
print("- **The pose contract becomes exact on every standing** if a tie rule that does not depend on the search removes the lug's "
      "posed growth at no native cost (@sec-oq-ties).")
print()
print("If none fires, the recommendation stands as written, with the bounds of this chapter attached.")
```
